summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on embedded software development and firmware experience across STM32 microcontrollers, NVIDIA Jetson, and Raspberry Pi. Builds bare-metal C/C++ device drivers and peripheral firmware (UART, SPI, I2C, GPIO, Bluetooth) alongside FreeRTOS task coordination for real-time embedded systems. Integrates computer vision and ML inference (CUDA, TensorRT, YOLO) into embedded pipelines, with additional depth in Linux systemd service management and TCP/IP networking for headless device deployment.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition device for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometer sensors with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth microcontroller firmware to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through firmware-level calibration and resolution tuning on embedded microcontroller hardware.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller temperature-monitoring firmware in bare-metal C, with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver on STM32 microcontroller hardware.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C/C++ (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 computer vision on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART device-driver-level serial communication.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on bare-metal embedded C firmware.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer device driver, alongside TensorRT-optimized YOLO computer vision (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) for visual servoing.

Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation) with static IP TCP/IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration; configured XRDP for remote embedded device administration.
